rationale: B wins because it finds the uglier, more reportable tension and tells the founder which angle to actually pitch first. "Allbirds shrinks its way to a first margin gain, but the losses haven't stopped" has a sharper thesis than A's accurate but flatter "Allbirds posts its first gross-margin gain after closing stores and cutting 40% of its products." A is strong work, but B's discipline in "Hold the product angle until wear-test data exists" is the difference between a useful angle set and a polite pile of maybes.
gaps_in_A: "Allbirds posts its first gross-margin gain after closing stores and cutting 40% of its products" is accurate, but it leaves the real tension in the body: still unprofitable, still below IPO price, one quarter of margin relief. That's the scar tissue a business reporter cares about.
"Story type: category-creation" is the wrong label for the shoe angle. One company durability claim with no test data is not category creation; it is an evidence challenge.

"making a wholesale partnership a centerpiece of its relaunch" overstates the supplied fact. The update says the partnership is part of the relaunch, not that the channel shift carries the whole comeback.
"three viable shapes exist. Pick one" is too generous. The margin angle is pitchable with numbers; the retailer and product angles are proof-starved until the partner and test data show up.
gaps_in_B: "The retailer betting shelf space on Allbirds' second act" assumes physical shelf or floor space from a fact block that only says retail wholesale partnership. If this is online, limited, or not in stores, that phrasing gets wobbly fast.
"Story type: customer-story" is clumsy. The wholesale partner is a buyer/channel protagonist, not a customer story in the usual PR sense.
"what the original got wrong" is a smart reporter question, but it risks implying a known failure mode for the original wool runner. The update only supplies a comparative durability claim.
"How large is the net loss this quarter, and what is the cash position?" is useful, but cash position is outside the provided facts. Fine as a question, not as a hidden premise.
